subject: Draft redlines: delivery title vs. training use — handoff
messages:
From: Elise Kim <elise.kim@brighttech.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: legal@brighttech.com
Date: 2026-06-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft redlines: MSA & Order Form — delivery title vs. training use

Hi Stephanie,

Attached are our initial redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. The two points we need clarity on before procurement can sign:

1) Delivery title vs. productization: the current draft assigns "title" to any generated output — BrightTech needs assurance we can use model outputs internally and externally without unexpected assignment to Redwood. We proposed language preserving customer use for productization (see MSA §3.2 in the redline).

2) Training / feedback license: procurement is asking for an explicit opt-out for training on customer payloads. Our legal team is OK with Redwood using telemetry/metrics for operations but not training models on PII or proprietary content.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept: (a) a carveout that keeps delivery title to the customer for outputs used in BrightTech products, and (b) an explicit training opt-out checkbox in the Order Form?

I've copied Mark (engineering lead) and BrightTech Legal for their awareness. We can schedule a short call if that's easier.

Thanks,

Elise Kim
VP Legal, BrightTech
elise.kim@brighttech.com

Attachments: BrightTech_MSA_redline_v3.pdf, BrightTech_OrderForm_Redline.xlsx

Elise — thanks for sending this over and for being explicit about the two asks. Looping in Jordan (contracts) and Ben (product ops) to coordinate language and feasibility. Quick read: both items are commonly requested, and we have precedent language that might map.

Action items I propose:
- Jordan: can you review the attached redline and suggest minimal edits to the MSA that maintain Redwood's ability to improve models while honoring a customer opt-out?
- Ben: please confirm operational constraints — e.g., whether telemetry-only (no training) mode is feasible, and what evidence we can provide (logs, telemetry reports).

If we can align on short language for the Order Form opt-out checkbox, we can move to procurement and get a signature-ready PDF. If not, let's schedule a 30-min call today.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-17T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: MSA & Order Form — delivery title vs. training use

Thanks for pulling this together. I reviewed BrightTech's redlines and propose the following path-forward (high level):

- Delivery title: we can accept a narrow, use-case-specific assignment that clarifies the customer retains title to outputs that are "embodied in a Customer Product" (definition) while Redwood retains rights to aggregate, de-identified model telemetry and quality measurements. Proposed textbook clause: "Customer retains title to Outputs to the extent incorporated into Customer Products, except that Redwood may collect and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement."

- Training opt-out / feedback license: offer a checkbox in the Order Form that triggers an operational flag (opt-out) on the tenant. When checked: (a) Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train models, (b) Redwood may still use non-content telemetry for infra metrics and SLO monitoring, and (c) Redwood will provide an audit log of calls flagged as opt-out where feasible.

A few open questions for product ops (Ben):
1) How long to implement the opt-out flag on a per-tenant basis and what guardrails for accidental inclusion?
2) What evidence artifact can we produce during procurement to give BrightTech confidence (e.g., exportable log of opt-out status + periodic telemetry reports)?

From a legal standpoint, this keeps Redwood's ability to innovate on model improvements via aggregated signals while honoring the customer's desire not to have raw data used for training. If BrightTech insists on a permanent assignment of training derivatives or additional restrictions on aggregated telemetry, we will need to escalate to pricing and likely offset via commercial concessions.

Jordan Blake
Senior Contracts Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, elise.kim@brighttech.com
Date: 2026-06-17T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: MSA & Order Form — delivery title vs. training use

Quick operational update from product ops:

- Opt-out implementation: we can implement a per-customer opt-out flag in our control plane within 2 sprints (approx 4 weeks) if prioritized. The flag will prevent forwarding customer payloads to any training pipelines and will exclude such calls from offline training datasets. It will not change live inference latency or standard caches.

- Evidence artifacts: we can provide (a) a tenant-level opt-out status export (CSV) and (b) a weekly telemetry summary showing token volumes and a confirmation that no training jobs referenced the tenant ids for the covered period. Producing cryptographic proof-of-exclusion is non-trivial and would require additional engineering effort scoped separately.

- Delivery title: from an ops perspective, we do not need customer title to manage the serving runtime. The only concern is downstream productization where BrightTech asks Redwood to indemnify third-party claims on derivative works — that is commercial and contract/legal should handle it.

If BrightTech needs the opt-out to be effective immediately upon signature, we can support a clause that delays any training-by-default window and honors opt-out from day-0. If the customer expects retroactive removal of prior training, that is operationally infeasible without a full retrain of models (and thus would require commercial compensation).

Proposed next step: Jordan to produce suggested redline text for the MSA and a one-liner Order Form checkbox. Stephanie, if you agree, I'll put example text in the shared Drive and prepare the opt-out report template.

Ben Carter
Head of Product Operations — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
